title: Must a shape with four right angles have equal opposite sides?
description: A four sided shape has all four angles equal to ninety degrees, and the video shows with two triangles that its opposite sides are equal. Keeko then writes the two triangles in the wrong letter order and asks whether that matters.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape with four right angles has equal opposite sides, so four right angles are enough to define a rectangle. Watch for students who write congruent triangles with the letters in any order instead of corner by corner.

source: ABCD has all four angles 90°. Show that AD = CB and DC = BA,
video_script.why: The child sees that four right angles are enough to force equal opposite sides, and that congruent triangles must be written with their corners in matching order.
video_script.substitution: Join B and D, list the equal parts of the two triangles, match them by AAS, and read off the opposite sides.
video_script.anchor: quadrilateral ABCD with four right angles and the line BD drawn across it
video_script.wrong_answer: triangle b eigh d is congruent to triangle c d b
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes triangle BAD is congruent to triangle CDB because the two triangles look the same; but the corners must be written in matching order, and the right angle is the middle letter A in the first and the first letter C in the second.
video_script.payoff_line: Opposite sides are equal, so eigh D equals C B and D C equals B eigh

final_answer.spoken: opposite sides are equal, so eigh D equals C B and D C equals B eigh

maths_rules: ABCD has angle A = angle B = angle C = angle D = 90 degrees; BD is joined
in triangle BAD and triangle DCB: angle BAD = angle DCB = 90 degrees, and BD is common
angle ABD + angle DBC = 90 degrees (angle B) and angle CDB + angle DBC = 90 degrees (triangle BCD), so angle ABD = angle CDB
AAS: triangle BAD is congruent to triangle DCB, with B matching D, A matching C and D matching B
matching sides: AD = CB and BA = DC
triangle CDB would match A with D, but angle A is 90 degrees and angle D of triangle CDB is not 90 degrees, so triangle BAD is not congruent to triangle CDB in that order
video_script.design: One idea: four right angles force equal opposite sides. Wrong idea: the letters of congruent triangles can be written in any order. The shape with BD stays on the board throughout.
